subject: biology
title: Absorption in the small intestine
key_idea: Digested nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine, which is lined with villi. Villi and the microvilli on their cells give a very large surface area. Each villus has a thin lining, a capillary network and a lacteal, so absorption is fast and efficient.

blocks.text: Absorption is the movement of digested food molecules and water into the blood. This section covers where it happens.

items: The **small intestine** is the region where nutrients are absorbed.
Most water is absorbed from the small intestine.
Some water is also absorbed from the **colon**.
Molecules pass into the blood by diffusion and by active transport.
Nutrients are absorbed in the small intestine.
Most water is absorbed in the small intestine, and some in the colon.

blocks.text: (Supplement) The inside of the small intestine is not smooth. It is covered in tiny finger-like folds that increase its surface area.

items.meaning: A tiny finger-like projection of the lining of the small intestine.
Tiny projections on the surface of the cells that line a villus.
A lymph vessel in the centre of a villus.

items: Villi and microvilli greatly increase the internal **surface area** of the small intestine.
A larger surface area means more nutrients can be absorbed in a shorter time.
The wall is a single layer of cells (epithelium), so the **diffusion distance** is short.
The cells have microvilli, which add more surface area.
A network of **capillaries** lies just under the surface.
A **lacteal** lies in the middle.
Villi and microvilli increase the surface area for absorption.
The villus wall is one cell thick, so substances cross quickly.

blocks.text: Each villus has two routes out. Which one a nutrient takes depends on what it is.

rows: Glucose, amino acids, water, mineral ions and water-soluble vitamins
Blood, then the hepatic portal vein to the liver
Fatty acids and glycerol (the products of fat digestion), and fat-soluble vitamins
Lymph, which later joins the blood

items: Blood in the capillaries carries absorbed molecules away, so their concentration stays low next to the villus.
A good blood supply keeps a **steep concentration gradient**, so diffusion continues.
Amino acids move into the capillaries, are carried in the plasma and reach the liver in the hepatic portal vein.

diagram.alt: A sorting activity. Absorbed substances are sorted into those carried away by the capillaries and those carried away by the lacteal.
diagram.prompt: Sort each substance into the vessel in the villus that absorbs it.

items: Capillaries absorb glucose and amino acids into the blood.
The lacteal absorbs fatty acids and glycerol.
A good blood supply keeps the concentration gradient steep.

checks.q: State where most water is absorbed.
checks.a: In the small intestine. Some is also absorbed in the colon.

checks.q: (Supplement) Explain why a villus has a wall that is only one cell thick.
checks.a: It makes the diffusion distance short, so nutrients are absorbed quickly.

checks.q: (Supplement) State the job of the lacteal in a villus.
checks.a: It absorbs fatty acids and glycerol, the products of fat digestion, and carries them away.

worked_example.question: The small intestine is lined with many villi and is adapted to absorb glucose. Describe and explain how the structure of a villus is adapted for its function.
answer_points: Microvilli provide a large surface area.
The epithelium (lining) is one cell thick, so diffusion is fast.
Diffusion of glucose takes place across the lining.
A good blood supply maintains a steep concentration gradient.
worked_example.tip: Any four score one mark each. Pair each structure with what it does.

worked_example.question: Some people have a condition called coeliac disease. In this condition the body reacts to eating gluten, a protein found in wheat. This reaction damages the villi in the small intestine. Explain how the undamaged villi are adapted for their function.
answer_points: They have a large surface area.
Capillaries and a blood supply maintain the concentration gradient.
They absorb digested food molecules, vitamins and minerals.
A lacteal absorbs and transports fats.
The wall is thin, one cell thick, with capillaries close to the surface.
This gives a short diffusion path and rapid diffusion.
